findings.title: Do not republish an invalidated query when adding an organization search
findings.body: The existing query is read before this branch invalidates the key and samples a new revision. If a concurrent IdP update invalidates the login cache between those operations, this constructor carries the old query's result sets into an entry published with the post-update revision and current counter. For example, moving an IdP from organization A while another request adds a search for organization B can permanently restore A's stale membership. Subsequent login searches can then offer an IdP belonging to another organization. Preserve previous results only after verifying their revision is still valid, or cache organization searches independently.

findings.title: Evaluate invalidation against stored eligibility, not organization-aware enabled state
findings.body: The original model comes from getById(), whose organization-aware wrapper reports isEnabled() as false when the organization is disabled. However, the login cache is populated through the JPA delegate using the IdP's stored enabled flag, so it can contain enabled public IdPs from disabled organizations. Changing such an IdP to hidden, link-only, or non-public makes both predicates false here and skips invalidation, even though the stored query membership changed. Cached getForLogin() calls consequently continue returning the now-ineligible IdP. Compare the original persisted eligibility fields rather than the organization-aware enabled state, and cover updates while an organization is disabled.

findings.title: Clean up the actual aliases created by the test
findings.body: Every cleanup callback targets the literal alias `alias`, but the loop creates providers named `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`. The callback at line 425 repeats the mistake for `idp-alias-20`. These callbacks therefore attempt to delete a nonexistent or unrelated provider instead of the test fixtures, potentially producing 404 failures during teardown and leaving realm-level providers behind. Register cleanup using each provider's actual alias.
